headline: Funding flows. Partnerships form. Silence looms.
deck: This week, cash continues to fuel the space race while strategic partnerships emerge amidst a backdrop of silence and uncertainty.

stories.head: True Anomaly raises $190M for co-orbital security
stories.body: True Anomaly secured a $190 million Series C funding round, now valuing the company at $1.6 billion. This influx of capital is aimed at enhancing their co-orbital security and space domain awareness capabilities, which are increasingly in demand from the Department of Defense. As the Pentagon looks to bolster its defenses, True Anomaly is well-positioned to capitalize on government contracts.
stories.soWhat: In a sector where cash often equals credibility, True Anomaly's funding suggests they're not just surviving; they might be thriving in a crowded market.

stories.head: Look Up and Skynopy automate collision avoidance
stories.body: Look Up and Skynopy have partnered to develop an automated satellite collision avoidance service, a necessity as the number of satellites in orbit continues to grow. The service aims to streamline operations and enhance safety for commercial and government satellites alike. With the increasing congestion in space, this collaboration could serve as a model for future partnerships in the industry.
stories.soWhat: If there's one thing we can count on, it's that the space traffic jam is only getting worse; automating collision avoidance might be the only way to keep things from going off the rails.

stories.head: $1.4B boost for space resilience in FY27 budget
stories.body: The FY27 budget markup has allocated an additional $1.4 billion to enhance space resilience, reflecting growing recognition of the importance of securing U.S. interests in space. This funding is likely to support various initiatives aimed at countering threats from adversaries and ensuring operational continuity. With geopolitical tensions rising, the U.S. is clearly prioritizing its space capabilities.
stories.soWhat: In a world where space is becoming a battleground, this funding might just be the tip of the iceberg; expect more dollars to flow as the stakes get higher.

watchlist.title: True Anomaly's next moves post-funding
watchlist.body: With $190M in the bank, True Anomaly's strategic decisions will be closely watched as they seek to expand their footprint in co-orbital security.

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
